data_disclaimer: Descriptive soil profiles used to explain a VISUAL image estimate. A photograph cannot measure NPK, pH, electrical conductivity or micronutrients. Laboratory soil testing provides accurate nutrient and pH values. The numeric thresholds below only tune the demo image heuristic and can be edited freely.
limitations: A photograph alone cannot determine exact NPK values
A photograph alone cannot determine soil pH
A photograph alone cannot determine electrical conductivity or salinity
A photograph alone cannot determine micronutrient concentrations
Camera white balance, shadow, flash and time of day change the apparent colour of the same soil
A wet soil always looks darker than the same soil when dry, which can imitate a different soil class
improve_photo_tips: Photograph in indirect daylight, not under a harsh shadow and not with flash
Fill the frame with soil - avoid grass, hands, tools or sky in the shot
Hold the camera roughly 30 to 40 cm above a freshly turned patch of soil
Include a small flat area of levelled soil rather than a lumpy clod pile
Take one dry-surface photograph and one at root depth for comparison

black.label: Black Soil
black.visual_description: Very dark grey to near black, often with a smooth or slightly shiny surface. Shows wide cracks when dry and becomes very sticky when wet.
general_properties: High clay content with high water-holding capacity
Slow internal drainage
Generally rich in calcium and potassium, often low in nitrogen and organic matter
Swells when wet and shrinks and cracks when dry
black.sugarcane_suitability: Widely used for sugarcane in the peninsular belt. Drainage management is the key requirement.
management_notes: Ensure drainage channels are open before the monsoon
Work the soil only when it is at the right moisture - it is unworkable when wet and hard when dry
Add organic matter to improve structure and reduce cracking
Avoid heavy machinery on wet black soil to prevent compaction
black.irrigation_note: Holds water for a long time. Irrigate less frequently but check that water is not standing.

red.label: Red Soil
red.visual_description: Reddish-brown to rust coloured, from iron oxide content. Usually looks lighter and more granular than black soil.
general_properties: Light to medium texture with moderate drainage
Often low in nitrogen, phosphorus and organic matter
Can be slightly acidic in some regions
Lower water-holding capacity than black soil
red.sugarcane_suitability: Sugarcane can be grown with assured irrigation and good organic matter management.
management_notes: Add organic matter every season to raise water-holding capacity
Use more frequent, smaller irrigations
A soil test is particularly valuable, as phosphorus is often limiting
Mulching with trash reduces surface evaporation
red.irrigation_note: Dries out faster than black soil. Shorter irrigation intervals are usually needed.

sandy.label: Sandy Soil
sandy.visual_description: Pale yellowish to light brown with a visibly grainy texture. Individual particles are often distinguishable in a close photograph.
general_properties: Very high infiltration and very low water-holding capacity
Low natural fertility and low organic matter
Nutrients leach rapidly below the root zone
Warms up quickly and dries quickly
sandy.sugarcane_suitability: Possible only with assured, frequent irrigation and a strong organic matter programme. Drip irrigation is a major advantage here.
management_notes: Prioritise organic matter - it is the single most effective amendment
Use frequent small irrigations rather than heavy flooding
Use the maximum practical number of nutrient splits
Consider drip irrigation and fertigation if available
sandy.irrigation_note: Needs the shortest irrigation interval of all the classes. Heavy single irrigations mostly drain away.

clay.label: Clay Soil
clay.visual_description: Greyish-brown to brown with a smooth, dense, sometimes polished-looking surface. Forms hard clods when dry.
general_properties: High water-holding capacity and slow drainage
Good nutrient retention
Prone to waterlogging, surface crusting and compaction
Difficult to work at the wrong moisture level
clay.sugarcane_suitability: Suitable where drainage is properly managed. Waterlogging is the main risk to the crop.
management_notes: Maintain open drainage channels
Avoid working or driving on the field when saturated
Add compost to improve aeration
Consider raised beds or ridge planting where waterlogging recurs
clay.irrigation_note: Long irrigation intervals. Check for standing water after each irrigation.

loamy.label: Loamy Soil
loamy.visual_description: Medium to dark brown with a crumbly texture. Neither as dark as black soil nor as pale and grainy as sandy soil.
general_properties: Balanced sand, silt and clay fractions
Good water retention with adequate drainage
Good nutrient-holding capacity
Generally the easiest texture to manage
loamy.sugarcane_suitability: Generally regarded as the most favourable texture for sugarcane.
management_notes: Maintain organic matter with compost or green manure
Follow the standard local split fertilizer schedule
Routine drainage maintenance is usually sufficient
loamy.irrigation_note: Moderate irrigation intervals. Follow the schedule from the irrigation module and verify by hand.

mixed.label: Mixed / Unknown
mixed.visual_description: The image did not match any single class clearly. This can happen with mixed soil, unusual lighting, wet soil, or a photograph containing non-soil objects.
general_properties: Not determined from this image
mixed.sugarcane_suitability: Not determined. A laboratory soil test will give a reliable answer.
management_notes: Retake the photograph in indirect daylight, filling the frame with soil
Get a laboratory soil test for nutrient and pH values
Use the manual soil type selector on the recommendation form if you already know your soil type
mixed.irrigation_note: Check soil moisture by hand at root depth until the soil type is confirmed.

alluvial.label: Alluvial Soil
alluvial.visual_description: Light brown to greyish-brown, often with visible fine sand and silt. Texture varies widely along a river system, from sandy near the channel to clayey further out.
general_properties: Deposited by rivers, so texture and fertility vary over short distances
Generally fertile, with good potassium and lime, often low in nitrogen and organic matter
Usually well drained with good moisture retention in the loamier variants
The most extensive and agriculturally important soil group in India
alluvial.sugarcane_suitability: Among the best soils for sugarcane. The Indo-Gangetic alluvial belt of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar is India's largest sugarcane growing region.
management_notes: Texture varies within a single field - check drainage in more than one spot
Nitrogen is usually the limiting nutrient; follow a split schedule
Add organic matter to maintain structure under continuous cropping
Sandier patches need shorter irrigation intervals than clayey ones
alluvial.irrigation_note: Moderate intervals in loamy alluvium; shorten them noticeably on the sandier variants.

dry.label: Dry appearance
dry.note: The surface looks pale and light with no darkening from moisture. Confirm by hand at root depth - the surface can be dry while the root zone is still moist.

moderate.label: Moderately moist appearance
moderate.note: The surface shows some darkening consistent with moisture. This is a visual impression only, not a measurement.

wet.label: Visibly wet appearance
wet.note: The surface looks dark and saturated, possibly with a sheen. Check that water is not standing, especially in clay and black soils.

low.label: Low apparent organic matter
low.note: Light colour with little visible plant residue. Consider adding well-decomposed compost or farmyard manure. Confirm with a laboratory organic carbon test.

moderate.label: Moderate apparent organic matter
moderate.note: Some darkening and visible residue. Maintain current organic matter practice.

high.label: High apparent organic matter
high.note: Dark colour with visible residue. Note that dark colour can also come from moisture or from a naturally black soil, so this is not a reliable organic carbon reading.
